simple.meaning: מְדוֹר (mᵉdôwr) is a Hebrew word meaning “a dwelling.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מְדוֹר (H4070) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:11, with occurrences in Daniel.

definitions.full: H4070. medor [ מְדוֺר ] noun [masculine] dwelling place ; — suffix מְדֹרָךְ Dan 4:22 ; 4:29 , מְדוֺרֵהּ 5:21 . [ מְדָר ] noun masculine id.; — suffix מְָדרָהוֺן Dan 2:11 .

occurrences.englishText: It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”
it is you, O king, that have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.
At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.

He was driven from the sons of men, and his heart was made like the animals’, and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys. He was fed with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky; until he knew that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and that he sets up over it whomever he will.
